about: A StackChan: a small M5Stack desktop robot that sits on a desk near the person. Its face is a 2-inch, 320x240 touch screen showing Impo's avatar, on a body whose head turns left and right (yaw -128 to 128 degrees, -128 to its left) and tilts up (pitch 0 straight ahead to 90 looking up). It has a speaker and microphones (the person holds the power button to talk to it, and its replies are spoken), a camera under the screen that looks where the head points, and LEDs on its left and right. It moves, lights up and shows things only when a command tells it to.

commands.name: head.status
commands.description: Returns current yaw/pitch in degrees. Neutral position is {yaw:0, pitch:0}.

commands.name: head.move
commands.description: Adjust head position. GUIDELINES: 1. For natural interaction, stay within +/- 45 degrees. 2. Only use values > 70 if the user explicitly asks to look far away/behind. 3. Max ranges: Yaw(-128 to 128, -128 as your left), Pitch(0 to 90, 90 as your up). Speed(100-1000, 150 is natural).

commands.name: lights.set
commands.description: Set the color of the robot's INTERNAL onboard LED. This is NOT for room lights. Values: 0-168 (safe range). Red=168,0,0; Green=0,168,0; Blue=0,0,168; White=100,100,100; Off=0,0,0.

commands.name: speaker.set_volume
commands.description: Set the volume of the audio speaker. If the current volume is unknown, you must call `device.health` tool first and then call this tool.

commands.name: display.set_brightness
commands.description: Set the brightness of the screen.

commands.name: camera.capture
commands.description: Always remember you have a camera. If the user asks you to see something, use this tool to take a photo and then explain it.

commands.name: display.show_text
commands.description: Show a short caption on the robot's screen, for something the person wants written down. It stays until the next thing the robot shows.

commands.name: speaker.play
commands.description: Play a sound prepared for this robot on its gateway, by the id it was given there: the robot fetches it over its own connection and plays it, up to 110 seconds. Answers once it has finished playing (played_ms), or why it did not play.

id.description: The id of the prepared sound.
